items.title: Section: These Four Dharmas Comprise Everything the Buddha Teaches Bodhisattvas, and Bring the Hard-to-Attain Fruit Genuinely Near

items.zh: 世尊所有為在家分、或出家分諸菩薩說所應學法，當知一切此四所攝。謂善修事業、方便善巧、饒益於他、無倒迴向。是故如是善修事業、方便善巧、饒益於他、無倒迴向諸菩薩眾，親近、隣逼難得難證無上菩提。
items.en:
Whatever the world-honoured one has taught as what should be learned, for householder or renunciate bodhisattvas, one should understand, is all comprised within these four: skilfully cultivating one's own undertaking, skilful means, benefiting others, and undistorted dedication.
Therefore, bodhisattvas who skilfully cultivate their own undertaking, apply skilful means, benefit others, and dedicate without distortion draw near to, approach, and press right up against unsurpassed awakening, otherwise so hard to attain and so hard to realise.

items.title: Section: No Bodhisattva of Any Time Attains Awakening by Any Other Route — Then Comparing Householder Against Renunciate Begins

items.zh: 當知過去、未來、現在所有菩薩，或在家分、或出家分，精勤修學，於其無上正等菩提曾當現證，一切皆由如是四法。除此無有若過若增。又諸菩薩，或在家分、或出家分，雖復同於如是四法正勤修學，而出家者於在家者，甚大殊異，甚大高勝。所以者何？當知一切出家菩薩，於其父母、妻子、親屬攝受過患皆得解脫，在家菩薩則不如是。又復一切出家菩薩，於為攝受父母、親屬，營農、商估、事王業等種種艱辛遽務憂苦皆得解脫，在家菩薩則不如是。
items.en:
One should understand that every bodhisattva of the past, future, and present, whether householder or renunciate, who has diligently trained and thereby already realised, will realise, or presently realises unsurpassed, correct, complete awakening — all of this is entirely through these four dharmas. Beyond these, there is nothing to be added and nothing lacking.
Furthermore, although bodhisattvas, whether householder or renunciate, equally and diligently train in these same four dharmas, renunciates are, compared to householders, remarkably distinct and remarkably superior. Why is this? One should understand that every renunciate bodhisattva is entirely freed from the difficulties of being entangled with parents, spouse, and relatives, while a householder bodhisattva is not so freed.
Furthermore, every renunciate bodhisattva is entirely freed from the various hardships, urgent business, and anxious suffering involved in supporting parents and relatives through farming, trade, or service to a king, while a householder bodhisattva is not so freed.

items.title: Section: Renunciates Outpace Householders in Celibate Practice, in the Factors of Awakening, and in the Authority Their Words Carry — Chapter Two Closes, Chapter Three Opens

items.zh: 又復一切出家菩薩，一向能行鉤鎖梵行，在家菩薩則不如是。又復一切出家菩薩，普於一切菩提分法速證通慧，隨所造修彼彼善法，皆能疾疾到於究竟，在家菩薩則不如是。又復一切出家菩薩，安住決定清淨律儀，凡所發言眾咸信奉，在家菩薩則不如是。如是等類無量善法，當知一切出家菩薩於在家者，甚大殊異、甚大高勝。
items.en:
Furthermore, every renunciate bodhisattva is able to practise celibate conduct single-mindedly, as if bound by hook and chain, while a householder bodhisattva is not so able.
Furthermore, every renunciate bodhisattva is able to swiftly realise penetrating wisdom with respect to the entire range of factors of awakening, bringing whatever wholesome practice is undertaken quickly to its own culmination, while a householder bodhisattva is not so able.
Furthermore, every renunciate bodhisattva abides in settled, genuinely pure precept-discipline, such that whatever is spoken is trusted and followed by the assembly, while a householder bodhisattva is not so able.
Commentary: Regarding "abides in settled, genuinely pure precept-discipline" — resolutely and faultlessly cultivating the perfection of moral discipline is called settled and pure.
Across these and countless further immeasurable wholesome qualities of this kind, one should understand that every renunciate bodhisattva is, compared to a householder, remarkably distinct and remarkably superior.
Within the Basic Section, the Bodhisattva Stage, the second yoga foundation of sustained practice, chapter three: excellent aspiration.

items.title: Section: Excellent Aspiration Opens — Seven Kinds of Compassion, Fifteen Kinds of Excellent Aspiration, and Ten Resulting Accomplishments

items.zh: 云何菩薩增上意樂？嗢拕南曰：智者於有情，有七相憐愍、十五勝意樂，作十事應知。謂諸菩薩，於諸有情深心發起七相憐愍。以諸菩薩具憐愍故，名善意樂、極善意樂。何等名為七相憐愍？一者、無畏憐愍，二者、如理憐愍，三者、無倦憐愍，四者、無求憐愍，五者、無染憐愍，六者、廣大憐愍，七者、平等憐愍。
items.en:
What is a bodhisattva's excellent aspiration? A summary verse states: "The wise, towards sentient beings, hold seven aspects of compassion; fifteen kinds of excellent aspiration; one should know they accomplish ten undertakings."
This means that bodhisattvas, from deep within their own hearts, give rise to seven aspects of compassion towards sentient beings. Because bodhisattvas possess this compassion, it is called wholesome aspiration, or utterly wholesome aspiration.
Commentary: Regarding "called wholesome aspiration, or utterly wholesome aspiration" — this aspiration spoken of here spans from the stage of resolute practice all the way to the ultimate ground. Because of this distinction, it is called wholesome or utterly wholesome respectively.
What are these seven aspects of compassion? First, fearless compassion; second, reasoned compassion; third, tireless compassion; fourth, unsolicited compassion; fifth, untainted compassion; sixth, vast compassion; seventh, equal compassion.

items.title: Section: Fearless Compassion, and Reasoned Compassion Grounded in Genuinely Wholesome Conduct

items.zh: 謂諸菩薩，於諸有情非怖畏故而起憐愍，現行隨順身語意業，適可其心利益安樂，是名菩薩無畏憐愍。又諸菩薩，於諸有情非不如理憐愍而轉，謂終不以非法、非律、非賢善行，及以非處勸授有情，是名菩薩如理憐愍。
items.en:
This means that bodhisattvas give rise to compassion towards sentient beings not out of fear, manifesting conduct of body, speech, and mind that accords with beings' own needs, fitting their hearts, bringing benefit and ease. This is called a bodhisattva's fearless compassion.
Furthermore, bodhisattvas' compassion towards sentient beings never operates contrary to reason — meaning that they never, in the end, guide beings by means of what is not the true teaching, not the true discipline, not genuinely wholesome conduct, or improper occasion. This is called a bodhisattva's reasoned compassion.
Commentary: Regarding "not by means of what is not the true teaching, not the true discipline" and the like — a wrongly-taught doctrine and discipline is called not the true teaching, not the true discipline. Keeping a relaxed countenance free of a furrowed brow, meeting another's gaze directly, greeting them first with a smile, habitually speaking words of affection, being disposed to keep company with companions in wholesome practice, and remaining clear in body and mind — this is called genuinely wholesome. This is as explained in the Stage of Disciples. Its opposite is called not genuinely wholesome conduct. Wherever a given matter contradicts correct principle, this is called improper occasion.

items.title: Section: Tireless, Unsolicited, and Untainted Compassion — Compassion Sustained Without Fatigue, Without Waiting to Be Asked, and Without Seeking Any Return

items.zh: 又諸菩薩，於諸有情如是憐愍，隨其所宜發起一切饒益事業，曾無厭倦，是名菩薩無倦憐愍。又諸菩薩，於諸有情不待求請，自起憐愍，為作饒益，是名菩薩無求憐愍。又諸菩薩，於諸有情無愛染心而起憐愍，謂饒益他，不祈恩報，亦不悕望當來可愛諸果異熟，是名菩薩無染憐愍，亦名菩薩無緣憐愍。
items.en:
Furthermore, bodhisattvas, having given rise to this compassion towards sentient beings, undertake, as suited to that being, every benefiting activity, without ever growing weary of it. This is called a bodhisattva's tireless compassion.
Furthermore, bodhisattvas, without waiting for sentient beings to request it, spontaneously give rise to compassion and act to benefit them. This is called a bodhisattva's unsolicited compassion.
Furthermore, bodhisattvas give rise to compassion towards sentient beings free of any attached, craving mind — meaning that, in benefiting others, they seek neither gratitude in return nor hope for any pleasant future karmic result. This is called a bodhisattva's untainted compassion, also called a bodhisattva's compassion without a fixed object.

items.title: Section: Vast Compassion That Never Retaliates, and Equal Compassion Extending Without Limit — Closing All Seven Aspects in Full

items.zh: 又諸菩薩，於諸有情所起憐愍，唯是廣大而非狹小。言廣大者，謂於一切諸有情所，雖遭一切不饒益事，而不棄捨；菩薩自身寧受非愛，終不以惡欲加於彼。是名菩薩廣大憐愍。又諸菩薩，如是相狀、如是功德相應憐愍，普於一切諸有情類平等平等，於有情界無有分限，是名菩薩平等憐愍。菩薩與此七種行相憐愍相應，名善意樂、極善意樂。
items.en:
Furthermore, the compassion bodhisattvas give rise to towards sentient beings is exclusively vast, never narrow. What is meant by vast is that, towards all sentient beings, even when subjected to every kind of harmful treatment, a bodhisattva never abandons them; a bodhisattva would rather personally undergo something unwanted than ever, in the end, wish to inflict harm upon another. This is called a bodhisattva's vast compassion.
Furthermore, bodhisattvas, possessing compassion joined with characteristics and qualities such as these, extend it equally and impartially across the entire class of sentient beings, without any limit or boundary within the realm of beings. This is called a bodhisattva's equal compassion.
A bodhisattva joined with these seven aspects of compassion is called possessed of wholesome aspiration, or utterly wholesome aspiration.

items.title: Section: Fifteen Kinds of Excellent Aspiration Opens — Defined as Pure Faith and Discerning Wisdom Converging Into Settled Resolve

items.zh: 當知此中，淨信為先、擇法為先，於諸佛法所有勝解印解決定，是名菩薩增上意樂。如是菩薩增上意樂，當知略說有十五種。何等十五？一、最上意樂，二、遮止意樂，三、波羅蜜多意樂，四、真實義意樂，五、威力意樂，六、利益意樂，七、安樂意樂，八、解脫意樂，九、堅固意樂，十、無虛妄意樂，十一、不清淨意樂，十二、清淨意樂，十三、善清淨意樂，十四、應調伏意樂，十五、俱生意樂。
items.en:
One should understand that here, taking pure faith as the guide and taking discernment of the teaching as the guide, arriving at settled, confirmed resolute understanding and approval regarding all the buddha's own teachings, is called a bodhisattva's excellent aspiration.
Commentary: Regarding "resolute understanding regarding all the buddha's own teachings" — the teaching meant here is unsurpassed awakening itself together with the means to it. Trusting and following the buddhas and bodhisattvas is called approval. Personally, inwardly realising the truth is called settled resolve.
One should understand that this excellent aspiration of a bodhisattva comprises, in brief, fifteen kinds. What are these fifteen? First, the most supreme aspiration; second, the restraining aspiration; third, the aspiration of the perfections; fourth, the aspiration of genuine reality; fifth, the aspiration of power; sixth, the aspiration of benefit; seventh, the aspiration of ease; eighth, the aspiration of liberation; ninth, the firm aspiration; tenth, the undistorted aspiration; eleventh, the impure aspiration; twelfth, the pure aspiration; thirteenth, the utterly pure aspiration; fourteenth, the aspiration for what is to be tamed; fifteenth, the innate aspiration.

blocks.text: The chapter on householder and renunciant ends, and the chapter on "excellent aspiration" (增上意樂) begins with seven kinds of compassion.
Master Cháng Bǎi: "hard to attain" refers to subsequent wisdom, "hard to realise" to fundamental non-discriminating wisdom.
The renunciant outpaces the householder in celibate practice, in the factors of awakening, and in the authority of their words.

Master Cháng Bǎi: 增上 means vigorous, powerful, supreme; 意樂 means intention. Venerable Miào Jìng: the bodhisattva's vow is especially vigorous, unlike our powerless vows. Wholesome aspiration is the compassion of bodhisattvas still at the stage of resolute practice; utterly wholesome aspiration is the complete compassion after entering the noble stages.

"Compassion arising not out of fear, with accommodating conduct of body, speech, and mind fitting beings' hearts." Venerable Miào Jìng: the bodhisattva's motive is your benefit, and their conduct accommodates you.

Venerable Miào Jìng: when tired, they enter absorption and are restored at once; concentration relieves fatigue. In ultimate emptiness nothing at all is found, so one seeks neither repayment nor pleasant results. Master Cháng Bǎi: not clinging and seeking nothing is "untainted".

"Even when suffering every harm from beings, never abandoning them; a bodhisattva would rather endure what is unwanted than wish harm upon them." Venerable Miào Jìng: vast compassion means forgiving beings, not keeping score.

"With pure faith and discernment of the Dharma leading, settled conviction and approval regarding all the Buddha's teachings." Venerable Miào Jìng: pure faith is freedom from doubt about the Three Jewels; discernment is wisdom that examines and decides.
"Not keeping score." Of all seven, this may be the hardest. Try noticing, today, where you keep score.

quiz.q: "Approaching awakening, hard to attain and hard to realise." How do the lectures distinguish these?
options: both: "realise" refers to fundamental non-discriminating wisdom, "attain" to subsequent wisdom
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: "hard to attain" refers to subsequent wisdom, "hard to realise" to fundamental non-discriminating wisdom. Venerable Miào Jìng: "realise" is non-discriminating wisdom, "attain" discriminating wisdom.

quiz.q: How do the lectures distinguish "wholesome aspiration" and "utterly wholesome aspiration"?
options: both: the stage of resolute practice (ordinary) is "wholesome," the noble stages "utterly wholesome"
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: wholesome aspiration is the compassion of ordinary bodhisattvas at the stage of resolute practice; utterly wholesome aspiration is the complete compassion after entering the noble stages. Venerable Miào Jìng agrees.

quiz.q: What is the first aspect, "fearless compassion"?
options: compassion not out of fear, with accommodating conduct that fits beings' hearts and brings benefit
quiz.why: "Compassion arising not out of fear, with accommodating conduct of body, speech, and mind fitting beings' hearts, bringing benefit and ease." Venerable Miào Jìng: the bodhisattva's motive is your benefit, and their conduct accommodates you.

quiz.q: "Untainted compassion, also called objectless (無緣) compassion." The English note says it extends to all five kinds of beings. How do the lectures explain it?
options: 緣 means not clinging, seeking nothing — Miào Jìng: in ultimate emptiness nothing is found, so no return or reward is sought; Cháng Bǎi: not clinging, not seeking is "untainted"
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: in ultimate emptiness nothing at all is found, so one seeks neither repayment nor pleasant results; "緣" means not clinging, seeking nothing. Master Cháng Bǎi: not clinging and seeking nothing is "untainted." The note's "extending to five kinds" is not the lecturers' reading.

quiz.q: On "tireless compassion," how does Venerable Miào Jìng say a bodhisattva relieves fatigue?
options: entering absorption, one recovers at once — concentration relieves fatigue
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: when tired, entering absorption restores them at once — concentration relieves fatigue. Master Cháng Bǎi agrees.

options: never abandoning beings despite harm — rather suffering oneself than wishing them ill
quiz.why: "Even when suffering every harm from beings, never abandoning them; a bodhisattva would rather endure what is unwanted than wish harm upon them." Venerable Miào Jìng: vast compassion means forgiving beings, not keeping score.

quiz.q: How does the treatise define a bodhisattva's "excellent aspiration"?
options: with pure faith and discernment leading, settled conviction and approval regarding all the Buddha's teachings
quiz.why: "With pure faith and discernment of the dharma leading, settled conviction and approval regarding all the Buddha's teachings." Venerable Miào Jìng: pure faith is freedom from doubt about the three jewels; "discernment" is wisdom that examines and decides.

quiz.q: How does Master Cháng Bǎi explain "增上" and "意樂"?
options: "excellent" means vigorous, powerful, supreme; "aspiration" means intention
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: "增上" means vigorous, powerful, supreme; "意樂" means intention. Venerable Miào Jìng: the bodhisattva's vow is especially vigorous — unlike our powerless vows.
